title: I Printed the Picnic-Shelter Reservation After They Occupied My Permit

parts.text: I arrived at shelter B at 11:01 a.m. with a paid permit and a reunion was already on my grill. The kiosk said: PERMIT IN THE CLIP. FOUR HOURS. NO WALK-UP GRILLS. Reunion lead Hank waved a folding chair. "Family is a permit." I was thirty-seven, booker, holding a printed slot. I photographed the empty clip, the permit, and their coolers on my tables. Then I logged an occupy. At 11:09 parks asked why Hank's reunion was on shelter B without a clip. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Parks can see Hank's coolers on shelter B with an empty permit clip.

social.video_title: They grilled on my paid shelter without a clip — Part 1/2
social.description: Picnic shelter, a paid permit, and a reunion on my grill. I logged the occupy. Would you have shown the print?

parts.text: Hank called it shade until parks asked for the log. I printed the occupy, the photo, and the permit. They moved. Hank reserved a walk-up lawn and told the family shade was always about optics. Optics is a word reunions use when a cooler exists. Shelter policy now has a second line: FAMILY IS NOT A CLIP. I keep my four hours. Hank lawns. The grill finally looks like a reservation, not a takeover. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.

social.video_title: Family is not a clip — Part 2/2
social.description: Occupy log, moved reunion, and a second line. Was shade ever my permit?
